country.comment: Empirical investigation conducted in the urban district (Amphoe Muang) of Pathumthani province in the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, Thailand.

effect_estimate.comment: Pre-post (1998 vs. 2003) chi-squared comparisons of household survey data and PWA municipal administrative/technical records.
effect_estimate.value: Following the 1998 Pathumthani BOOT water supply privatisation (where PWA retained retail billing and progressive cross-subsidised national tariffs while contracting bulk production, network expansion, and maintenance to PTW), household metered piped water access in informal settlements rose from 28.0% in 1998 to 84.0% in 2003 (+56.0 percentage points, chi-squared = 47.727, p < 0.01), including increases from 11.8% to 85.3% (+73.5 pp, chi-squared = 36.796, p < 0.01) in small informal settlements and from 41.5% to 82.9% (+41.4 pp, chi-squared = 14.989, p < 0.01) in large informal settlements, outpacing formal communities (76.8% to 93.9%, +17.1 pp, chi-squared = 11.675, p < 0.01). Income-poor households (<=7,500 baht/month) saw piped access increase from 50.0% to 88.6% (+38.6 pp, chi-squared = 15.441, p < 0.01) vs. 57.7% to 90.0% (+32.3 pp, chi-squared = 35.128, p < 0.01) among income-non-poor households, while total PWA municipal household connections increased by 58.03% from 15,495 to 24,488. Informal-community households reported significant improvements in water clarity (+26.8 pp, chi-squared = 12.041, p < 0.01), drinkability (+14.7 pp, chi-squared = 4.086, p < 0.05), turbidity (+15.8 pp, chi-squared = 3.590, p < 0.10), 24-hour reliability (+12.6 pp, chi-squared = 3.384, p < 0.10), adequate pressure (+35.0 pp, chi-squared = 19.180, p < 0.01; PWA technical data: 2.4 to 4.0 bars), and same-day complaint response (+54.8 pp, chi-squared = 15.033, p < 0.01; PWA response time: 60-120 min to 15 min). Costs rose for a subset of informal-settlement households: the share paying <=2,000 baht for connection fell from 75.0% to 51.7% (-23.3 pp, chi-squared = 3.316, p < 0.10) and the share paying <=375 baht/month fell from 95.5% to 74.0% (-21.5 pp, chi-squared = 4.693, p < 0.05), though changes among income-poor households were not statistically significant (+1.5 pp for connection cost, chi-squared = 0.009; -16.1 pp for monthly charge, chi-squared = 1.455).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Directly documents the BOOT contractual structure (network expansion mandate, unbundled maintenance, PWA retention of progressive cross-subsidised billing) and empirically observes metered household connections, tariffs/fees, and complaint response across informal settlements lacking legal tenure, while bounded by the non-experimental design ceiling of 2.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Primary empirical component is a single-wave 2003 cross-sectional household survey (with retrospective recall of 1998 conditions by residents present since 1998) comparing poor/informal and non-poor/formal strata within a single privatised municipal district via chi-squared tests, triangulated with official municipal aggregates, without an unexposed/non-privatised comparator district or quasi-experimental design.

sample_size.comment: From 1,436 households across 10 sampled communities (out of 30 total communities in the study area), 288 households were targeted, 274 completed questionnaires were obtained, and 212 households meeting the >=1998 residency criterion were used in analysis, alongside municipal-wide PWA administrative/technical data.
sample_size.value: 212 urban households analysed (from 274 completed questionnaires out of 288 targeted households across 10 sampled communities: 86 households in 5 informal communities and 126 households in 5 formal communities); supplemented by PWA municipal records covering 15,495 household connections in 1998 and 24,488 household connections in 2003
sample_size.where_found: PDF p. 10, Section 4.1; PDF p. 12-13, Section 4.3 & Table 3; PDF p. 21, Table 6

study_design.comment: Single-district cross-sectional household survey in 2003 using retrospective recall of 1998 pre-privatisation status (with no unexposed control municipality), analysed with chi-squared tests of pre-post percentage changes across community/income poverty strata and compared against official 1998 and 2003 PWA municipal records and BOOT contract terms.
study_design.value: Cross-sectional household questionnaire survey (conducted in 2003 with retrospective recall of 1998 pre-privatisation conditions) using two-stage stratified systematic sampling across informal and formal communities, analysed via pre-post proportion differences and chi-squared tests across poor and non-poor groups and triangulated with official PWA pre/post administrative and technical water quality data
